title: RAW_UNSCREENED: gegenläufige Labelrichtung als Registerfunktion
summary: RAW_UNSCREENED: otedy is a label then a prose opener, while okal occurs in prose before a panel label; the pair may distinguish named-entry reuse from a forward address.

design.scope_description: Exact label/prose bridges on f77r/f82r/f83r from GDT790; no visual ownership expansion.
design.mechanism: Metatextual register layer assigns direction-sensitive functions: label-to-prose is a named entry, prose-to-label is an address/index.
design.unit: Exact otedy and okal label/prose bridge occurrences.
design.contrast: Direction-sensitive document function versus repeated caption/name use.
design.prediction: The direction model predicts different continuation obligations after otedy and before okal; a repeated-name model predicts the same nominal function in both directions.
concrete_observations: GDT790 records otedy as f77r.3 label and f77r.25 prose opener.
GDT790 records okal in two f82r prose records before its lower-pool label.
linked_consequences: otedy should introduce a body whose first field can be compared to the label form.
okal should point forward to a later panel record without requiring picture proximity to translate the word.
design.nearest_rival: Labels are repeated captions or learned names with no directional document function.
design.distinguishing_observation: Use only exact written order: test whether each bridge has the predicted body/address continuation and whether the opposite-direction rival requires the same written relation.
assumption_costs: label/prose status is known from GDT790
direction can be a document function
no pictured object is equated with a word meaning
design.strongest_likely_failure: Only a few bridges exist and both functions may be ordinary name reuse.
